confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from five web searches, mostly aggregator and cost-of-living pages (Numbeo-derived data, budget guides) that disagree with each other and are partly crowdsourced. Cheap-meal, beer and cappuccino figures are reasonably consistent: about 25,000–50,000 LAK for a cappuccino, 15,000–30,000 LAK for a Beerlao, and $1.50–3 for local meals. I found no direct Vang Vieng price for restaurant wine or for a mid-range dinner for two. Cocktail rests on a single guide range ($3–6). Wine is my estimate, set above cocktail because imported wine is costly in Laos. The mid-range meal comes from per-person kip ranges for tourist riverside restaurants, scaled to two people and three courses. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge of Vang Vieng's backpacker-to-resort market. I did not search or inspect any accommodation prices, so they are the least certain. The RBA rate was taken from a search-result summary of the RBA exchange-rate page (4:00 pm, 18 Nov 2026), not from a direct read of the page.
comparable_city_reasoning: Priced as a tourist-oriented Lao town. Local eateries are at Lao levels, while riverside bars and Western-style cafés run roughly 1.5–2.5 times higher. Accommodation is modeled on other low-cost backpacker hubs in northern Laos and Southeast Asia, such as Luang Prabang and Pai, with a premium for the riverside resort segment.
